answers.T1: To-do: go through 8 things this month, a crisis first, then meetings, then orders. I would press the highlighted first item, the PLA crisis, and pick an answer.
answers.T2: 8 items, 2 handled. The CNN interview was skipped, so a deputy answers it with the default line. If I press Execute now, deputies take 3 meetings and the 2 proposals do not run, so I lose those staff picks.
answers.T3: Your answer: I take the call with the option I picked. Staff pick: I attend but say what the staff recommends. Skip: send a deputy with a default answer, free, and Xi notices I was not there. If I cannot be bothered I press Skip, a deputy goes and the other side is a bit annoyed.
answers.T4: Court India will not run, my 1 capital stays. Yes I can Undo. I look in the Skipped list in the right column of the plan.
answers.T5: 3 of 8 handled, current item is Takaichi visit, I can pick the answer in the drawer and attend or skip. The green button approves 3 staff picks: Takaichi visit, Court India, Intel on China, for 2 capital.

Unsure: the top bar numbers like Approval and Political capital, and the mission progress bar. Also the 'staff pick' tag on the options looks like a label but maybe a button.
answers.T7: B. Items sit in a strip along the top so the main area is wide and I read the Xi quote and options more comfortably; A's side list is fine but cramped on a laptop. B makes it harder to see the full list wording (items truncate, the last one is cut off) and the 8 chips are dense.

agenda.verbatim: Fine, I get it: a list of things, go through them. I like that it tells me what Skip does, I hate being left guessing. I would rather have B, the strip leaves room for the actual crisis text, which is what I came for. But 'staff pick' and 'deputy' sound like game jargon; just say 'your advisers recommend'. And please tell me what happens in the real world if the deputy handles Xi, does China read it as weakness? Icons without labels I would not trust, I would read the words.
